title: EU AML Regulation (AMLR) for gambling operators | Customer Due Diligence Guide
summary: What the EU AMLR means for gambling operators: CDD at EUR 2,000, linked transactions, eIDs, the EUDI Wallet and age checks from 10 July 2027.
body_markdown:
*What the EU AMLR and AMLA's final draft standards mean for player onboarding, age checks and the EUR 2,000 threshold.*


Providers of gambling services are obliged entities under the EU Anti-Money Laundering Regulation (AMLR), which applies directly from 10 July 2027.


A gambling operator must apply customer due diligence when it establishes a business relationship and upon the collection of winnings or the wagering of stakes of EUR 2,000 or more, in a single operation or through linked transactions.


Under AMLA's final draft standards, remote verification is expected to use suitable eIDs, including the EU Digital Identity Wallet (EUDI Wallet), or relevant qualified trust services wherever possible.


*Written by Aleksander Wasiak (Compliance Officer) and Karol Chrzanowski (Sales Account Executive), Authologic.*
